perturbation.u: u_j=+1/8 for odd one-based j<=64, -1/8 for even one-based j<=64, and 0 otherwise

constants.source_lower_bound_requirement: Global boundedness below on R^1024 is not assumed in manuscript Section1.1; boundedness on compact C suffices.
constants.component_smoothness_proof: For signed Hadamard row v_i, Hessian f_i=v_i v_i^T-(5/4)uu^T. Its eigenvalues lie in [-5/4,1024], hence operator norm at most1024.

nonconvex_feasible_line.line: x(t)=x_s+t*u, -1/8<=t<=1/8; all points are nonnegative with l1 norm1

proof: For t=u^T x and multiplier lambda>=0 of sum x<=1, KKT is x_j=max(a_j+rho*t*u_j-lambda,0), with lambda(sum x-1)=0.
Each of the four coordinate groups P(32 positive-u), M(32 negative-u), B(64 negative-a), R(896 remaining) therefore has equal entries, either all positive or all zero.
B is zero because its right-hand response is -3/128-lambda<0.

If P and M are both positive, their coefficient difference is rho*t/4 and t=4 times that difference, so t=rho*t. Since rho=5/4, t=0. If lambda<1/128, the first64 alone have mass>3/2, infeasible. Thus R is zero; lambda cannot be0, so sum constraint is active and coefficients=1/64,lambda=1/64.

If P alone is positive with common coefficient z, t=4z and stationarity gives lambda=1/32-(3/8)z. If lambda<1/128, z>1/16, infeasible because32z>2. Thus R is zero; lambda>0 and mass constraint gives z=1/32,lambda=5/256. Inactive M has response (1-rho)z<0. The M-only case is symmetric.
If neither P nor M is positive, t=0 and their inactive conditions give lambda>=1/32. Then R is also zero, leaving x=0 while lambda>0, violating complementarity.

These exhaust the KKT points. A global minimizer exists by compactness and is stationary. x_s is not a local minimizer by the displayed feasible negative-curvature line. x_plus and x_minus have equal objective, hence both are global minimizers. Strict positive inactive KKT margins and positive Hessian on each active face imply strict local minima.

orthant_constraint_role.feasible_direction_on_C_alone: d=-e_j-x_plus for any j=65,...,128 (and analogously for x_minus)
orthant_constraint_role.consequence: x_plus and x_minus are not stationary on C alone, so the orthant indicator changes the optimization problem and remains meaningful.

exact_smoothed_stationary_branches.classification: Strict local minima on their support faces with strict inactive LMO margins; no global smoothed-minimum claim made.

oracle.sampling: Fresh independent uniform row index i in{1,...,1024}; row indices independent of the initial point.
oracle.finite_sum: f=(1/m) sum_i f_i, where f_i(x)=m(A_i x-B_i)^2-(5/8)(u^T x)^2 and m=1024
oracle.implementation_identity: For signed Hadamard row v_i of W diag(c), q_i(x)=v_i(v_i^T(x-a))-(5/4)(u^T x)u
oracle.variance_proof: E||v_i(v_i^T r)||^2=m||r||^2, E[v_i(v_i^T r)]=r, where r=x-a; the common deterministic concave-gradient cancels from centered noise.
oracle.noise_source: Uniform sampling of individual scalar data rows only; the concave term is evaluated exactly.

validation_method: Exact algebra using orthogonality and signed Hadamard rows, plus the unchanged groupwise KKT case split. Empirical numerical checks are recorded separately by run_demo.py.

data_matrix.column_signs: c=2*np.random.default_rng(20261014).integers(0,2,1024)-1; sampled once and fixed across all optimization seeds
data_matrix.a: entries1..64 are1/32; entries65..128 are -3/128; entries129..1024 are1/128
data_matrix.relation_to_previous_problem: Identical full gradient and Hessian; objective differs only by removal of constant1/8. Previous additive block noise is removed.

assumptions.C: Nonempty compact convex l1 unit ball; Euclidean diameter2.
assumptions.g: Indicator of D; proper lower-semicontinuous convex; prox_beta_g(x)=max(x,0).
assumptions.relative_interior_qualification: Vector with all coordinates1/2048 lies in ri(C) intersect ri(D).
assumptions.constraint_regularity: For x in C, x_+ lies in C intersect D and dist(x,C intersect D)=dist(x,D)=||x_-||, so kappa=1.
assumptions.initial_point: For each seed, x0=-e_J with J uniform over1024 coordinates and independent of future oracle draws; x0 belongs to C.
assumptions.exact_lmo: s=-sign(v_j)e_j, j=first argmax|v_i|; s=0 if v=0.
assumptions.schedules: gamma_k=(k+1)^(-3/4), beta_k=(k+1)^(-1/4), alpha_k=(k+1)^(-1/2); all prefactors1; momentum initialized from first sample.
assumptions.random_initialization_interpretation: Apply estimates conditionally on x0; bounds above are uniform over C and thus remain valid after averaging over initialization.

certificates.H: max_(v in C intersect D) <z,x-v>=<z,x>+max(0,-min_j z_j)
certificates.averages: Every pre-update iterate included: (1/N) sum_(k=0)^(N-1) G_k, |H_k|, delta_k. Across-seed means and descriptive +/-2 standard-error bands.
certificates.slope_guide: N^(-1/3) is a comparison reference only. It does not change the exponents or claim a new theorem.
certificates.source_bound: The supplied Proposition2.11 with p=3/4,q=1/4,r=1/2 gives O(N^(-1/4)) for the expected averaged smoothed gap.
certificates.output_rule: The source expectation-selected index is not approximated by a per-path minimum or last iterate. Long runs report the averaged gap directly; no exhaustive row-history enumeration is attempted.
